ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback and for choosing a Weber grill!  Your grill should easily reach 500F, which is hot enough to cook and sear.

If your grill is not getting to that temperature, there are a few things to check. Let's start with the easy stuff:

1.) Please make sure you consider "High" on your control knobs to be the first spot to your left (the 9:00 position). The further you go to the right the lower the temperature will be and all the way to the right is low.

2.) Please make sure you're always cooking with the lid down except when flipping the food halfway. The second you open the lid the heat escapes, and you'll need to close it to let the temperature recover.

3.) It sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it reduces the pressure. 

Perform a soapy water leak test to check for leaks. If there is no leak, follow these instructions to reset the bypass safety mode. This is not only the reset, but how you want to light your grill each and every time.

Open the lid
Make sure all knobs are in the off position
Turn your LP tank on all the way
Wait 60 seconds
Turn the first burner to start/high
Hit your igniter
Turn on remaining burners one at a time and set each to high
Close the lid
Let your grill preheat to 500-550°F

Our Specialist team is here to help. Please look for our email outreach soon. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText: The quality is what I expect from Weber. I use my grill once or twice a week and it works flawlessly. Two things I would address if I was Weber is to affix the plastic “hubcaps” so they do not easily fall off the wheels, and put a set of wheels on the non-wheeled side of this model. Without the wheels, the unit gets lifted up by the droppable side table to wheel it around and eventually the hinge fails and you have to lift up the greasy grill body to move it. It would be nice if they offered a wheel kit for the non-wheeled side, or strengthened the metal to withstand the lifting. There is no fix offered by Weber. If your grill remains stationary, this will not be a problem.

Results.ReviewText:
So far, I really like my Spirit II E-210 LP Gas grill. I’ve followed manual suggestion to allow for a 10-min preheating with gas set on max gas flow. This has worked great as temperature is sufficiently high for a great sear on steaks, burgers, etc. 

From a design standpoint, I love the lack of sharp edges or corners on the side shelves. Most grills I’ve owned had sharply squared off edges. These present almost guaranteed spots to rip grill covers, especially during winter seasons where the cold weather tends to make grill covers less flexible, and therefore prone to tears. The Spirit II has rounded, smooth plastic corners which should go a long way to prevent tears. 

I have a feeling that I’m going to get a lot of excellent use from this grill for a very long time.
Results.Title: GOOD LOOKS, GREAT HEAT CONTROL & FRIENDLY DESIGN
